summary: This Robespierre lecture supplies the prophet-scapegoat middle layer of the French Revolution sequence: taboo breach and regicide create no-return solidarity, inherited mythology keeps operating inside reason's revolution, and Robespierre absorbs guilt so Napoleon can inherit revolutionary energy.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: sacrifice in war energizes the people, terrifies enemies, and breaks taboo so there is no way back.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The public Taboo page already uses this source for the no-retreat mechanism: once regicide and revolutionary sacrifice occur, compromise and surrender are removed.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Robespierre becomes the scapegoat who takes guilt for the nation so the people can move on.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The existing Taboo anchor already carries Robespierre as the secular scapegoat form of transferred guilt and purification.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: even a revolution of reason still runs on inherited mythology and makes the nation a new God.
existing_lens_links.rationale: This source extends the atlas relation from Rousseau's reason-as-religion setup into the Robespierre middle stage where mythic roles and national sacredness organize action.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Treat this source as already-public support for taboo breach, regicide as no-return point, public sacrifice as revolutionary energy, and scapegoat purification.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Taboo owns Robespierre when the active mechanism is breach, sacrifice, no-return solidarity, scapegoat purification, and transferred guilt. Reason As Replacement Religion owns the secular-sacred substitution; Legitimacy Fiction owns Napoleon's later Caesar/messiah role.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use this source as the Robespierre continuation of the French Revolution religious-substitution sequence: reason formally rejects priest, king, and nobility, but mythology still acts as society's subconscious operating system.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Reason As Replacement Religion gets the inherited sacred function inside secular revolution. Religion As Administrative Filter should not absorb this unless the source is selecting officeholders by a code; this lecture is about mythic role, sacrifice, and national sacredness.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Preserve this as the necessary precursor to the Napoleon layer already public on Legitimacy Fiction: Robespierre's sacrifice releases the revolutionary hurricane that Napoleon will later personify as Caesar and messiah.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Legitimacy Fiction owns the later role that keeps producing action. Robespierre stays primarily Taboo/Reason unless the active claim is the Napoleon myth that must keep moving.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Keep the 'new God is the nation-state' line as bounded national-sacredness pressure before later Nation sources formalize citizen-war mobilization and nationalism.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Nation owns the collective sacred body and citizen-war machinery. This source supports that body only secondarily; its main lens pressure is taboo breach and scapegoat purification.

new_lens_seeds.title: Revolutionary Role Sequence
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: A revolution of reason still requires religious roles: prophet, scapegoat, messiah, prince, and executor. The role sequence can move energy from Rousseau's promised land, through Robespierre's purification, into Napoleon's mythic action.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: The same pattern may compare Robespierre/Napoleon with later Lenin/Stalin/Marx pressure, but the public map can route the active mechanisms through existing concepts until the Napoleon impact file closes the French Revolution middle layer.
new_lens_seeds.boundary_note: Hold as a routing seed only, matching the merged revolutionary-role boundary review. Do not create a public page or lens-point ID until Napoleon has its own impact record and the sequence proves a mechanism that cannot be handled by Taboo, Reason, Legitimacy Fiction, and Power.

new_lens_seeds.title: Faith Executes Itself
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: Prophetic or revolutionary actors do not need certainty that the role is true; doubt can intensify the act of faith when the actor submits to a destiny the social mythology requires.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: This may help compare Robespierre's acceptance of death with later sacred-role, agency-loss, and revolutionary-executor material, but it is not yet distinct enough for a public page.
new_lens_seeds.boundary_note: Route to Eschatology only when sacred role-script is active, and to Free Will only when the issue is agency, submission, or chosen destiny. Do not promote a standalone faith-executes-itself page from this source alone.

chronology_notes.note: This April 24, 2025 lecture sits between the April 22 Rousseau/reason lecture and the Napoleon lecture. It should be treated as the middle prophet-scapegoat layer: Rousseau imagines the promised land, Robespierre purifies and takes guilt, Napoleon later turns the released mythology into action.

The semantic bundle flags a likely date issue around the king and queen's attempted flight: the lecture transcript says June 20-21, 1792, while historical context suggests Varennes in 1791. Do not build public chronology on that date without checking the source wording.

Jiang identifies Robespierre's last speech as July 26, 1794 and frames his death as a conscious submission to destiny; the impact belongs to mythic role and scapegoat transfer, not to a standalone Robespierre biography.
